key_insight: Stacked LCUs introduce a single tuning knob, the number of layers, that lets you trade off trainability against classical simulability instead of treating them as irreconcilable opposites.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers a practical way to choose variational ansätze that balance optimization stability with implementation and simulation cost on near-term hardware.
method: Build a stacked linear-combination-of-unitaries variational ansatz (S-LCU).
Analyze the Free Fermion S-LCU using diagrammatic methods.
Use layer count l to tune the trade-off between cost concentration and computational complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a variance lower bound of Ω(1/(n k^{3l})) and a classical simulation cost of O(k^{2l} n^3), versus quantum gate complexity of O(lkn^2).
watch_item: The favorable trainability guarantees are derived for the Free Fermion S-LCU setting, so broader performance may change for more general ansätze or hardware-noisy implementations.
paper_title: Stacking the Deck: Tunable Trainability in Stacked LCUs
